options: A report listing only cash transactions for the month
A legal document required to open a bank account
A report listing every account in the general ledger with its ending balance, split into debit and credit columns
A forecast of next year's revenue
questions.explain: A trial balance lists every general ledger account and its ending balance, confirming that total debits equal total credits.

questions.q: What does it mean when a trial balance's two column totals match?
options: Every transaction was definitely recorded to the correct account
The company is profitable this period
No adjusting entries are needed
Total debit balances equal total credit balances across the entire ledger
questions.explain: A matching trial balance confirms only that total debits equal total credits — the fundamental double-entry check.

questions.q: A company accidentally debits 'Office Supplies' instead of 'Equipment' for a $5,000 purchase, but still credits Cash $5,000. Will the trial balance catch this error?
options: Yes, the trial balance will be out of balance by $5,000
No — the trial balance will still balance perfectly, because both sides remain mathematically equal
Yes, but only if the amount is over $10,000
The trial balance cannot be prepared if any account is used incorrectly
questions.explain: A balanced trial balance cannot detect which accounts were used — it only confirms arithmetic equality between debit and credit totals.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the relationship between a balanced trial balance and 'correct books'?
options: A balanced trial balance is a necessary condition for correct books, but not a sufficient one
A balanced trial balance guarantees the books are completely correct
A balanced trial balance has no relationship to whether the books are correct
A balanced trial balance only matters for tax filings, not for accuracy
questions.explain: Balancing is required for correctness but doesn't guarantee it — wrong-account errors can still balance perfectly.

questions.q: Why would a trial balance report still be useful inside a fully automated system like Oracle Fusion General Ledger?
options: Because automated systems never need any sanity checks
Because Oracle Fusion cannot generate financial statements without it
Because it remains one of the fastest checks available before closing a period or generating financial statements, and is often the first thing pulled when troubleshooting
Trial balances are not actually used in modern ERP systems
questions.explain: Even with automation, a trial balance remains a standard, fast sanity check and is often a consultant's first troubleshooting step.
